1.word_for_word: नागं सप्तदशे — in the seventeenth chapter, the serpent; नागालयं तं निरयापयत् — he caused him to depart to the abode of the serpents; बन्धून् स्व-दुःखतः श्रान्तान् — his kinsmen exhausted by their own distress; सुप्तान् तत्र — sleeping there; दवात् अपात् — he protected from the forest fire; असमञ्जसम् — improper, disagreeable; अप्रियम् — unpleasant
1.translation: In the seventeenth chapter he caused the serpent to depart to the abode of the serpents, and he protected from the forest fire his kinsmen who, exhausted by their distress, had fallen asleep there. ‘Asamañjasam’ means improper or disagreeable—something unpleasant.

2.word_for_word: उपहार्यैः — with articles to be offered; भक्ष्यैः — edible offerings; सर्प-जनैः — by the serpent people; वानस्पत्यः — belonging to the lord of the forest, the tree; वनस्-पतेः मूले देयः — to be given at the foot of the tree; नागानां तद्-बाधा-परिहाराय — for the serpents' avoidance of that affliction; बलिः — tribute or offering; निरूपितः उपकल्पितः — prescribed, arranged
2.translation: ‘Upahāryaiḥ’ means edible articles to be offered. The offering was made by the serpent people. ‘Vānaspatya’ means an offering connected with the lord of the forest: the tribute prescribed to be given at the foot of a tree so that the serpents might be spared that affliction.

3.word_for_word: ते च नागाः — and those serpents; स्वं स्वं भागं जनैः दत्तम् — each one's portion given by the people; सुपर्णाय प्रयच्छन्ति — they hand over to Garuḍa; ततः भीताः — being afraid of him; गोपीथाय — for protection; रक्षणाय — for preservation
3.translation: Those serpents, being afraid of Garuḍa, would each give him the portion that the people had offered. ‘Gopīthāya’ means for protection, for preservation.

4.word_for_word: विष-वीर्याभ्यां यः मदः — the arrogance produced by his poison and strength; तेन आविष्टः — possessed by it; काद्रवेयः — a son of Kadrū; गरुडं कदर्थी-कृत्य — treating Garuḍa with contempt; अविगणय्य — disregarding him; यद् वा — or; सुपर्ण-भक्ष्यैः — as food for Garuḍa; एकैकः नागः दीयते — one serpent at a time is given; स्वं स्वं भागं सर्वे नागाः प्रयच्छन्ति — all the serpents give their respective portions; कालियः तु न प्रयच्छति — but Kāliya does not give his; अन्यैः दत्तम् अपि बलिं स्वयं बुभुजे — he himself ate even the tribute offered by the others
4.translation: Kāliya, a son of Kadrū, was possessed by the pride born of his poison and strength; he treated Garuḍa contemptuously and paid him no regard. Alternatively, the passage may mean that the tribute prescribed for Garuḍa consisted of the serpents themselves as his food, one serpent being supplied at a time. All the serpents would give their respective shares to Garuḍa, but Kāliya would not give his; instead, he himself ate even the offering supplied by the others.

6.word_for_word: विषम् एव आयुधं यस्य — whose very weapon was poison; प्रत्यभ्ययात् — he went forth against him; योद्धुं प्रतिजगाम — he advanced to fight; उच्छ्रित-नैक-मस्तकः — with many heads raised; उन्नमित-अनेक-फणः — with many hoods lifted; दद्-आयुधः — having teeth as weapons; दन्त-आयुधः — armed with fangs; कराल-जिह्वः — with a terrible tongue; उच्छ्वसित-उग्र-लोचनः — whose fierce eyes were expanded and glaring
6.translation: His very weapon was poison. He advanced against Garuḍa to fight, raising his many heads and hoods. ‘Dad-āyudha’ means one whose teeth are weapons, armed with fangs. He had a terrible tongue and fierce, expanded, glaring eyes.

7.word_for_word: तार्क्ष्य-पुत्रः — the son of Tārkṣya; गरुडः — Garuḍa; मधुसूदनस्य आसनं यस्मिन् — he upon whom Madhusūdana has his seat
7.translation: ‘The son of Tārkṣya’ is Garuḍa, he upon whom Madhusūdana has his seat.

8.word_for_word: तस्य गरुडस्य अगम्यम् — inaccessible to that Garuḍa; अगाधतया — because of its great depth; दुरासदम् — difficult to approach
8.translation: That place was inaccessible to Garuḍa and, because of its great depth, difficult to approach.

12.word_for_word: लेलिहः — one who licks/flicks his tongue; सर्पः — the serpent; अतः तत्र आवात्सीत् — therefore he took up residence there
12.translation: ‘Leliha’ describes the serpent as flicking or licking with his tongue. For this reason Kāliya took up residence there.

13.word_for_word: जाम्बू-नदम् — jāmbūnada gold; सुवर्णम् — gold; तेन अलङ्कृतम् — adorned with it
13.translation: ‘Jāmbūnada’ means gold; the object was adorned with that gold.

15.word_for_word: लब्धेहाः — having recovered activity; लब्ध-चेष्टाः — having regained movement
15.translation: ‘Labdhehāḥ’ means that they recovered their activity, that they regained movement.

16.word_for_word: नगाः — trees; वृक्षाः अपि — even the trees; पूर्वं शुष्काः सन्तः एव — although they had previously been dried up; विरूढाः — sprouted again
16.translation: ‘Nagāḥ’ here means trees. The sense is that even the trees which had previously dried up sprouted again.

17.word_for_word: ते विप्राः — those brāhmaṇas; ऊचुः — spoke; १७.१८ — the explanation carries through verses 17–18
17.translation: Those brāhmaṇas spoke; this construction carries through verses 17–18.

19.word_for_word: नष्ट-लब्ध-प्रजा — she whose people/children had been lost and regained; नष्ट-प्राया — as though nearly lost; पुनः लब्धा प्रजा यया — by whom her offspring had been obtained again
19.translation: ‘Naṣṭa-labdha-prajā’ describes one whose offspring had seemed virtually lost and had then been recovered again.

20.word_for_word: श्रमेण च कर्षिताः — exhausted and emaciated by fatigue; उपकूलतः — at the edge of the bank; कूल-प्रान्ते — on the margin of the riverbank
20.translation: They were worn out by fatigue. ‘Upakūlataḥ’ means at the edge of the bank, on the margin of the riverbank; the explanation extends through verse 23.
